release: fix the Windows x86_64 build and let every target build to the end (#1038)

* release: install the 32-bit loader for the Windows x86_64 build

Mozilla's Wine runs midl.exe through /lib/ld-linux.so.2, which comes
from libc6-i386. The Windows x86_64 builder only ever had it because
installing clang-18 from apt.llvm.org pulled it in. #886 removed that
step, and the explicit 32-bit install runs only for non-x86_64 arches,
so the next release failed at the first IDL file in accessible/:

    /lib/ld-linux.so.2: could not open

Install it for every Windows target. The regression test runs the
workflow's install step for each Windows entry in the build matrix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* release: build every target even when one fails

Only a release builds Windows, macOS and arm64, and the first failed
build cancelled the rest, so each release run could report at most one
broken target. publish-browser still needs every build to succeed, so a
failed target still publishes nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

getter-cost-parity: fail the renderer strings only when they skip the round trip (#1039)

RENDERER and UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL cost stock's synchronous round trip
to the GPU process, and that cost changes between browser sessions in
stock and Camoufox alike. The worker already left them out for that.
In the page, main's run after #1038 read stock at 15.0 and 20.6 us and
Camoufox at 31.3 and 35.0, just over the 2x bound, and the same code had
passed on the pull request an hour earlier. A local run read Camoufox at
12.0 and 20.0 us for the two strings in one session.

The spoof adds only a memoized lookup after the round trip, so a cost
above stock's says nothing about it. What the guard is there to catch, a
spoof that skips the round trip, still fails: it would read a few
hundred ns against stock's microseconds.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
